conviction_note: Lovesac's own Q2 guide, and therefore the -$0.39 consensus, contains only $3.6m of its $20.8m accepted IEEPA refund claim, while every same-quarter-end importer that has already reported collected the bulk of its claim inside exactly the 10-Jun-to-2-Aug window; sized at roughly a third of the 16% median historical reaction because the timing (Q2 versus Q3 receipt) is the one thing I cannot verify.

findings.finding: Lovesac told the June 11 call it had been accepted for $20.8m of IEEPA tariff refunds but had only received $3.6m, and put only that $3.6m in the Q2/FY27 guide; CBP-wide data show the payout wave ran through exactly Lovesac's fiscal Q2 (May 4 - Aug 2), with >50% of the $166bn pool repaid by July 10 and ~64% certified by Aug 21, so ~$8-15m of unguided COGS credit plausibly landed in the quarter being reported.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus of -$0.39 sits inside the company's guided net loss of -$3m to -$7m, which by the CFO's own statement excludes everything beyond the $3.6m already in hand; only two estimates cover the name, so nobody has re-marked the model for two and a half months of CBP disbursement. If the market had done the arithmetic, a $17m residual claim on a $240m equity with $57m of cash and $51.7m of unused buyback authorisation would not sit alongside the most extreme 25-delta skew in the day's universe (+30.5), a 24.85 put/call open interest ratio and 20.8% of float short. Lovesac's Q1 10-Q applies a gain-contingency model, so the credit is recognised on receipt, not accrual - which is precisely why the amount is invisible until the print.
findings.independence: Three separate filers with overlapping quarters confirm the payout timing: Williams-Sonoma, same Aug 2 quarter end, says 'substantially all of our initial refund claim of $197.8 million has been collected as of August 2, 2026' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000719955/000071995526000203/exhibit991fy2026q2earnings.htm); Bob's Discount Furniture recognised $37.9m in its quarter ended June 28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002085187/000162828026054345/bobs-20260628.htm); Arhaus had $37.8m in hand by Aug 6 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/06/3340012/0/en/arhaus-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results.html). Lovesac's own 10-Q corroborates the $3.6m through June 10 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1701758/000162828026042366/love-20260503.htm). Note the Arhaus release is also the source for finding 2 - treat those two as one source cluster for that leg only.
findings.notes: Lovesac's guided Q2 gross margin of 57.5-58.5% on $157-166m of sales already embeds ~2.2pp from the $3.6m; a further $10m would be ~6pp of margin and would turn a guided -$4m-to-+$2m adjusted EBITDA into roughly +$6m to +$12m.

findings.finding: Arhaus, reporting the overlapping calendar quarter on Aug 6, posted comparable written sales +12.5% (against +4% delivered) and raised full-year guidance, describing demand as accelerating during the quarter - a materially better category backdrop than existed when Lovesac set its Q2 guide on June 11 with only five weeks of the quarter elapsed and a Q1 comp of -1.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: LOVE is down 8.2% over 20 days and 22% off its 52-week high through a window in which its closest listed comp raised guidance on accelerating written demand; if the read-across were in the price the two would not have diverged, and the puts would not be bid 30 vol points over the calls. Written orders are a leading indicator that no aggregator maps onto a $240m microcap with two estimates.
findings.independence: Partial only - the same Arhaus release is the third corroborant in finding 1's source cluster, so the scorer should collapse that overlap. Independent of Arhaus, Lovesac's FY27 guide of $700-740m implies H2 of $400-440m against $398.3m of H2 FY26 actual (FY26 $697.1m less H1 of $138.3m + $160.5m), i.e. the low end of the full-year guide needs only +0.5% - the back-half bar is far lower than the headline range suggests (https://investor.lovesac.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/161/the-lovesac-company-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2026).

findings.finding: The material weakness is gone: the Q1 FY27 10-Q filed June 11 concludes disclosure controls were effective as of May 3, 2026 and reports no changes in internal control over financial reporting, so the restatement/remediation tail that this name has carried since the FY23 freight understatement is no longer a live disclosure item going into the fiscal-Q2 10-Q.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an absence, and absences never get written up - no wire story runs on a controls paragraph that reverted to boilerplate. It matters only because the CFO who signed that paragraph resigned four days later (8-K, June 15, with the unusual pre-emptive line that the separation 'is not related to any financial or accounting issues'), which is exactly the fact pattern that makes a reader assume the controls problem is still live when the filing says it is not. Worth a small positive because it removes a downside tail an anxious tape would otherwise price.
findings.independence: The June 15 8-K disclosing the CFO change and stating no financial or accounting cause is a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1701758/000121390026068869/ea0294793-8k_lovesac.htm

findings.finding: A comedian's Aug 18 TikTok about a Sactional arriving in 24 boxes, and the CEO's mocking reply, ran to roughly 10 million views and 14,000 comments and drew Fast Company and Inc. coverage in early September, with the company walking it back - a brand event entirely inside fiscal Q3 that will be the most-asked question on a call about a quarter it cannot have affected.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a consumer-media story, not a financial one, and no sell-side note or preview has connected it to the Sept 10 print; the stock is actually up 5.0% over the five sessions spanning the peak of the backlash, which is what tells you no equity holder has marked it. Small and two-sided: for a brand with low unaided awareness, ten million views of the product being discussed may be net neutral, and the sign is genuinely uncertain - which is why the band spans zero.
findings.independence: Second outlet, same event, different reporting: https://www.inc.com/victoria-salves/comedian-viral-joke-lovesac-24-box-couch-assembly-was-not-problem-company-response-was/91395357

searched_and_found_nothing: Live material weakness or open remediation plan in the fiscal 2027 filings - the Q1 FY27 10-Q reverted to effective-controls boilerplate, so the brief's controls door is a dead end (recorded as finding 3 instead)
Any 8-K, press release or investor-conference appearance between June 15 and Sept 9 in which Lovesac updated the $20.8m refund figure - EDGAR shows no 8-K after June 15 and no Item 7.01

Insider signal - the only post-print activity is a routine 15,000-share ($249k) Rule 144 sale by director Vineet Mehra on 2026-07-16 and RSU grants to the incoming CFO; no cluster, no open-market buying
Costco roadshow location counts - Lovesac's own roadshow page adds locations weekly with no historical series, so a point-in-time count is uninterpretable against any baseline
Promotional depth as a demand tell - the Sept 8-13 Labor Day event is tiered (40% on Sac bundles, 20% on Sactionals), which matches prior-year structure and is Q3 anyway
A usable straddle - the ATM bid-ask is 146% of mid on 3,645 total open interest, so there is no option-implied move to net the findings against

Section 232 furniture tariff changes inside the quarter - the 25% upholstered-furniture rate has been in force since Oct 2025 and scheduled step-ups are deferred to 2027, so nothing changed versus what the June guide assumed
Hiring-page or job-posting evidence of a team being added or cut
baseline_tension: My primary finding cuts directly against the baseline: the option market is paying 30.5 vol points more for puts than calls with a 24.85 put/call OI ratio and 20.8% of float short at 12.4 days to cover (MarketBeat, settlement 2026-08-14), and the specific thing I found is an under-guided cash windfall that would turn a guided loss quarter into a profit into that positioning - only the small TikTok item agrees with the skew.
